title: DC-area forecast: Clouds increase before remnants of Hurricane Isaias arrive tonight
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Increasing clouds today with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s. Showers from the remnants of Isaias could arrive as early as 8 p.m.

What’s next? Breezy Sunday with numerous showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms. Sunshine gradually returns Monday, with dry weather into midweek.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: More clouds than we'd like, but at least the rain holds off for daytime outdoor plans before showers move in tonight. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Saturday): Clouds increase through the afternoon. Highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s, with light winds from the northeast around 5 to 10 mph shifting from the east later in the day. Confidence: Medium

Tonight: Clouds and humidity increase as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias approach. Spotty showers could arrive as early as 8 p.m., first in southern areas, before becoming more numerous and widespread after midnight. Overnight lows dip into the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Sunday): Cloudy skies with waves of showers in the morning, becoming more scattered and intermittent during the afternoon and evening. A few thunderstorms could develop later in the day, and a brief, weak tornado cannot be ruled out, especially southeast of DC. Storm rainfall totals should average around 1.5 inches, though amounts could range from an inch to nearly 3 inches. Humid highs reach the mid- to upper 60s, with winds from the east around 15 to 20 mph and gusts of 25 to 30 mph. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Spotty showers continue overnight before tapering around dawn. Humid lows dip into the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

A mix of sun and clouds returns Monday, after a possible lingering shower early as Isaias moves farther away. It stays muggy, with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s. Winds from the northeast around 15 to 20 mph could gust to 25 mph. Confidence: Medium

Sunny skies and warmer temperatures return Tuesday as highs climb into the mid-70s to near 80. Humidity eases a bit, but it remains somewhat muggy, with dew points in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

Skies remain mostly sunny Wednesday, with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s. The next chance of showers arrives in the evening. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for October 10

A rare October 1979 snowstorm brought the earliest measurable snowfall on record, disrupting travel and knocking out power with heavy, wet flakes.
